body_markdown:
Aston Martin’s newest model only has two cylinders, but the company isn’t returning[to the city car segment](https://www.hagerty.com/media/automotive-history/12-of-the-most-memorable-aston-martins-and-one-best-left-forgotten/) . Developed jointly with Brough Superior, the new Aston Martin AMB 002 Roadster stands out as the British company’s first street-legal motorcycle.


We clarified “street-legal” because this isn’t the first time Aston Martin has released a two-wheeler. It launched[a superbike called AMB 001](https://www.hagerty.com/media/motorcycles/aston-martin-partners-with-brough-superior-for-100-futuristic-amb-001/) in 2019, and it unveiled a follow-up called the AMB 001 Pro in 2022, but both models were designed only for track use. The AMB 002 Roadster is aimed at a wider audience, with an equivalent level of luxury and performance to[Aston Martin’s road cars](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/driven-2026-aston-martin-db12-s-amplifies-the-grand-touring-formula/) .


Designed and engineered on a blank slate, the AMB 002 Roadster looks fast even when it’s parked. It’s characterized by sporty proportions, wind-sculpted lines, and a carbon-fiber fairing that underlines the effort that went into keeping weight in check. It’s every bit as dramatic as a supercar, yet the styling is more functional than it might seem. The gills cool the engine, for example.


Aston Martin’s 113-year heritage permeated several aspects of the AMB 002 Roadster. The side strakes seen on many of its recent cars run right below the bike’s handlebars and stretch across the front to underline the headlight. The blade-shaped rear light design is inspired by[the Valkyrie](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2023-aston-martin-valkyrie-first-drive-hypercar-apex-predator/) and[the Valhalla](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/aston-martin-valhalla-1079-hp-of-driving-heaven/) , among other models, while the short, thin saddle features leather upholstery.

Power comes from a new, water-cooled 1.1-liter V-twin engine rated at 130 horsepower and 81 pound-feet of torque. That might not sound like much; a Nissan Sentra posts higher figures, but keep in mind that the AMB 002 Roadster tips the scale at about 420 pounds. Cast in that light, it offers a supercar-like power-to-weight ratio. The engine was tuned to deliver low- and mid-range torque, and it sits on a titanium frame milled from solid billet. This weight-saving part helps unlock a 50:50 weight distribution.


Aston Martin is relatively new to the motorcycle world, so Brough Superior provided a lot of the technology packed into the AMB 002 Roadster. Beyond the engine, which was designed, machined, and assembled in Brough Superior’s French headquarters, the company fitted a double-wishbone front suspension system called Fior Fork that separates steering and braking forces to deliver better handling. There’s an anti-dive function, too, which helps keep the AMB 002 Roadster stable under heavy braking.


Built by hand, the Aston Martin AMB 002 Roadster is limited to 300 units globally. Pricing hasn’t been announced yet. It won’t be cheap, but it will certainly be more affordable than one of Aston’s limited-edition cars, like[the Valen](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/aston-martin-valen-powers-into-pebble-beach/) , priced at roughly $2 million.
